title: How Long Is a Coastline? Fractals and the Limits of Measurement
question: Why does the measured length of a coastline keep growing as the ruler gets smaller, and what does that say about nature's geometry?
summary: Lewis Fry Richardson found that coastline length depends on the ruler used. Mandelbrot turned the paradox into fractal geometry, revealing that roughness at every scale is a fundamental feature of the natural world.
